meta.title: Open Physics Problems Map
meta.description: Curated, multi-source catalog of open problems in physics with AI tractability estimates, cross-links, and landscape maps.

primary_sources.name: Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in physics
John Baez Open Questions in Physics FAQ
Clay Mathematics Institute Millennium Prize Problems
Coley: Open problems in mathematical physics (arXiv:1710.02105)

ai_tractability_rubric.high: Formal proof, mechanism from existing data, or computational theory problem where AI reasoning/simulation can plausibly close or nearly close the problem.
ai_tractability_rubric.medium: AI can accelerate theory/model selection substantially, but decisive progress needs new experiments or facilities.
ai_tractability_rubric.low: Empirically gated or underdetermined; AI helps explore theory space but cannot decide alone.
ai_tractability_rubric.none: Requires new discovery-class experiments, Planck-scale access, or is not uniquely decidable by science as currently framed.

agentic_10day_rubric.assumption: Strongest multi-agent harness: tool-using LLMs, code exec, literature search, formal provers, simulators, human-level verification at end of day 10. No new colliders or megaton detectors.

scores.sprint: Credible full closure, community verdict, or decisive partial with publishable success criterion in ≤10 days.
scores.stretch: Ambitious but imaginable with god-tier agents; more likely strong partial than final close.
scores.multi-sprint: Right shape for AI eventually; not honest as a single 10-day solve.
scores.not-agentic: Empirically gated, underdetermined, or century-scale formal; agents can only annotate/rank.

what_counts_as_solved: Peer-checkable proof or derivation of the stated claim
Reproducible data reanalysis that community would accept as closing an anomaly
Mechanism consensus with decisive out-of-sample prediction already satisfied by public data
Explicit meta-closure: show the Wikipedia 'open' item is already solved in literature
what_does_not_count: A confident blog post without code/proof

problems.name: Theory of everything
problems.summary: Is there a single coherent framework that unifies all fundamental interactions and explains all physical phenomena?
problems.why_hard: Requires reconciling quantum field theory with general relativity and matching all low-energy data.

agentic_10day.success: N/A
agentic_10day.why: TOE.
agentic_10day.viral_hook: If your agent claims TOE in 10 days, it's lying.

problems.name: Dimensionless physical constants
problems.summary: Can the dimensionless constants of nature (fine-structure constant, mass ratios, etc.) be derived from first principles, or are some historical/quantum accidents?

agentic_10day.why: No accepted principle selects observed values; may require multiverse/anthropic reasoning or a TOE.

problems.name: Anthropic principle necessity

agentic_10day.why: Blurs physics and philosophy; hard to falsify cleanly.

problems.name: Quantum gravity
problems.summary: Can quantum mechanics and general relativity be realized as a fully consistent theory? Is spacetime continuous or discrete? Graviton-mediated or emergent?

agentic_10day.success: N/A
agentic_10day.why: Planck-scale.

problems.ai_notes: Theoretical consensus may crystallize via holography/quantum info arguments; full QG still needed.
problems.name: Black hole information paradox
problems.summary: Do black holes radiate thermally as Hawking predicted? Does radiation encode interior information? What remains after evaporation?

agentic_10day.success: Map consensus islands (islands, holography) vs remaining gaps — not full QG.
agentic_10day.why: Theoretical progress possible as synthesis.
agentic_10day.viral_hook: Where does information go when black holes die?

agentic_10day.success: N/A for full Clay problem in 10 days. Possible: formalize statement + survey barriers in Lean.

agentic_10day.viral_hook: Don't claim NS in 10 days. Formalize the battlefield.
